analysis:
All changes are documentation only. No code, endpoint or deployment changes were supplied.

- encryption.md (patch hunk at ~107-118): the KEK model for the SSD cache (T-041, TB-007) gains two modes. Ad hoc signed builds get `key_unavailable` unless an ephemeral key is explicitly allowed. DEBUG builds can derive the KEK from the file `DARKBLOOM_DEBUG_CACHE_KEY_FILE` (`SSDDebugCacheKeyFile.swift`). The T-041 mitigations still assume a Secure Enclave-rooted KEK and K_lookup, so one low-severity finding is recorded. The release-build exclusion is asserted in prose and cannot be verified from the supplied evidence.
- prefix-cache.md: the supplied head units (lines 445-881) are mostly unchanged surrounding text. The changed hunk (lines 129-153) adds an unregistered GLM sparse-state candidate section, but its text is not visible in the supplied units. That section says SSD cache eligibility defaults on for `EigenLabs/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-NVFP4-mtp` via `PrefixCachePolicy.isGLM5NextDefaultModel`, with `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0` as the opt-out. This touches the T-041 per-donation gating and default-on posture. The patch excerpt is truncated, so I did not assess whether GLM stays outside coordinator-registered serving.
- glm53-flash-native.md (new, 131 lines) is only metadata here. Its text is not visible, so artifact trust, weight-hash and A-004/T-012/T-027 implications are not reviewed.
- design/README.md only adds an index link.

Next pass should read the full prefix-cache.md hunk and glm53-flash-native.md. It should also check the code behind `SSDDebugCacheKeyFile` and `isGLM5NextDefaultModel` if it is available.

findings.detail: The new text at encryption.md lines 110-118 documents a DEBUG-build path (`DARKBLOOM_DEBUG_CACHE_KEY_FILE`, `SSDDebugCacheKeyFile.swift`) that derives the SSD cache KEK from an on-disk file. It also documents an explicitly allowed ephemeral-key mode for ad hoc signed builds. The file-derived key is protected only by ownership, mode 0600 and volume encryption, not by the Secure Enclave. T-041 and its mitigations still treat every key as SE-rooted: K_lookup is derived from the SE-rooted KEK, a KEK wipe is the cryptographic purge, and lookup names are unfindable without the KEK. A key file that is readable, copied or backed up lets a disk observer or operator recompute the HMAC lookup tags and decrypt DBK3 files. That would reopen the leak #2 class that the HMAC design closed. The claim that release builds do not contain this path rests on code not supplied here, so the exclusion is unverified. Fix: update T-041 to record the debug and ephemeral KEK modes and the tag-recomputation and decryption exposure from the key file. Also state the build-time exclusion from release artifacts as a mitigation with a verification reference, such as a release-binary symbol check.
findings.title: Debug file-derived cache KEK is not in the threat model, which still says the KEK is SE-rooted
